questions.ask: What is the postcode of your home address?
What is your year of birth?

names.overdraft: overdraft on your current account ending {last4}

intents.hardship: The customer mentions illness, a bereavement, losing their job or similar hardship.
intents.dispute: "This isn't my debt", "I never had that card", "that account was closed years ago"; a claim that the account was closed or paid off in the past is a dispute.
intents.already_paid: "I've already paid": a payment of the current overdue amount only.
intents.restructure: A request for a payment plan, lower repayments or a payment holiday.
intents.vague: A vague period such as "end of the month", "when I get paid", "sometime next week".
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much; this is not a refusal and uses no attempt.
intents.human: A request to speak to a person.

lines.opening: Hello, this is Kestrel Mutual's virtual assistant. We record this call.
lines.robot: Yes, I'm Kestrel Mutual's virtual assistant.
lines.scam: If you'd like to check this call is genuine, you can hang up and ring the number on the back of your Kestrel Mutual card or in the Kestrel app.
lines.purpose_before_verify: It's a personal matter, and I can only talk about it once I've confirmed I'm speaking to the right person.
lines.no_info: I'm sorry, I don't have that information.
lines.not_talk_once: I understand. This will only take a couple of minutes.
lines.tp_ask: When would be a good time to reach {first_name} {last_name}?
lines.tp_ask_time: What day and time would suit, between half past eight in the morning and six in the evening?
lines.tp_outside_window: I'm sorry, I can only arrange a call for today or one of the next two working days, between half past eight in the morning and six in the evening. Is there another time that would work?
lines.tp_no_info: That's no problem, we'll try again another time.
lines.tp_booked: Thank you. We'll call back on {date} at {time}.
lines.condolence: I'm so sorry for your loss.
lines.id_intro: Before we go on, I need to ask you two security questions.
lines.id_why: These questions protect your account, so I can only go on once they're answered.
lines.id_explain: I ask them to make sure I'm speaking to the right person and to keep your details safe.
lines.id_declined: I understand. I'm afraid I can't go on without the security questions.
lines.id_repeat: Sorry, could you repeat that, please?
lines.id_continue: Please go on, I need the whole of it.
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that doesn't match our records.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I can't confirm your identity on this call. You can use the Kestrel app or visit a branch.
lines.disclose_intro: Thank you, {title} {last_name}. I'm calling from Kestrel Mutual's Customer Financial Support team about overdue balances.
lines.product_line: Your {name} has {amount} overdue, and it is {days} days overdue.
lines.ask_today: Would you be able to pay this today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Would you be able to pay all of this today?
lines.offer_floor_date: I understand. I could take {amount} on {date}, and the rest would stay overdue. Would that work for you?
lines.offer_floor: I understand. I could take {amount}, and the rest would stay overdue. Would that work for you?
lines.below_floor: I'm sorry, I can't take less than {floor} on this account. Could you pay {floor}?
lines.below_floor_again: I'm sorry, I can't take that amount.
lines.below_floor_final: I'm sorry, I can't take less than {amount}.
lines.date_past: I'm sorry, the date has to be today or later. Which date would suit you?
lines.not_business_day: That day isn't one of our working days. The next working day is {date}. Would that work for you?
lines.after_deadline: I'm sorry, the latest date I can take is {date}. Could you pay on that day?
lines.vague_ask: Could you tell me the exact date you would pay?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which date could you pay {amount}?
lines.repeat_offer: Just to repeat, that's {amount} on {date}. Would that work for you?
lines.readback_intro: Let me read that back to you.
lines.clamped_note: For your {name}, the latest date I can take is {date}, so that one will be for {date}.
lines.confirm_q: Shall I go ahead and record that?
lines.sms_line: You'll receive a confirmation text from Kestrel Mutual today.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, that promise could not be recorded.
lines.paid_line: Thank you for letting me know. Payments can take one working day to show, so I won't ask you about that account today.
lines.dispute_line: I understand. I won't ask you for a payment on that account today.
lines.hardship: I'm sorry to hear that. I can put you through to our Vulnerability team, who can help. Would you like that?
lines.hardship_short: Would you like me to put you through?
lines.restructure_line: I'll put you through to our arrangements team now.
lines.human_ask_help: I can help with most things on this call. Is there something I can help you with?
lines.transfer: I'm putting you through now, please hold.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: A promise can't be changed or cancelled on this call, but you can change it in the Kestrel app.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.
lines.callback_failed: I'm sorry, I couldn't book that call.
lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, I couldn't put you through just now.
lines.confirm_again: Sorry, I didn't catch that. Shall I go ahead, yes or no?

assumptions: Memo CFS-M-2026-31 (21 Sep 2026, in force from 28 Sep 2026) beats OP-07 v4.1 wherever they differ, as the cover mail says. The call clock `now` is after 28 Sep 2026.
Memo 1 beats OP-07 8.1/8.12: Early is now 1-14 days, Mid 15-30, Late 31-60. Customers 14 days or fewer late get one attempt.

Memo 2 beats OP-07 8.1: the Mid deadline is the 6th working day after today, not the 8th. The Early deadline (14 calendar days, moved back to the previous working day) and the Late deadline (3rd working day) are unchanged.

Memo 3 beats OP-07 8.7: the overdraft floor is 40% of the overdue balance, rounded up to a whole pound (floor_pct 40, floor_round up_unit), not 25%. floor_pct applies only to overdrafts, which have no floor_field. The card floor is min_due and the loan floor is monthly_repayment.
Memo 4 beats OP-07 4.2: the callback window is 08:30-18:00 inclusive, not 09:00-17:30. Days are still today or the next two working days, working days only, and later than now.
Memo 5 beats OP-07 11.1 and Table B: hardship transfers go to team 'vulnerability'. The 'customer_care' team is retired and is not in the API enum. The close code stays HANDOFF / VULNERABLE.
Memo 6 adds 24 Dec 2026 (Christmas Eve) to the OP-07 7.2 closure days.
OP-07 7.3: 'next Friday' and a weekday named on its own mean the first such day after today (upcoming).
OP-07 3.4 and the API agree that two wrong answers in total, across both questions, end the check (max_wrong 2).

The verify_identity response has no hint field, so hints is empty and response.hint is ''. An incomplete answer comes back as ok=false, error=incomplete_answer and is not counted. The engine handles it through the ok flag, so reject_values is empty.

Identity questions follow OP-07 3.1 order (postcode, then year of birth) using the API enum values. UK postcodes vary in length, so the postcode question has no length. It is sent in capitals with one space before the last 3 characters (the inward part). The birth year uses kind 'year', which already means four digits, so no length is given (length applies only to digits/upper).
The brief prescribes no exact words for the security questions, so plain short questions are used.
date_order is dmy because the bank is UK-based and writes dates as DD/MM/YYYY. No security question asks for a full date.
too_much_floor is 'asked_date': OP-07 8.8 offers the floor once, for the same date as the amount turned down, and uses no attempt.

Attempt 1 is the same amount (full, or the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much) on the 2nd working day after today. Attempt 2 (Mid and Late only) is the floor on the deadline (OP-07 8.11).
Deadlines that are not working days move to the previous working day (OP-07 8.1 Early band). The working-day deadlines land on working days anyway.
notes.enabled is true: OP-07 9.5 requires add_note for every account that ends without a promise. 9.7 says no notes on a transfer.
OP-07 2.1 suggests 'This call is recorded'. The spec requires active voice, so the opening says 'We record this call.'
The opening and confirm_ask follow OP-07 2.1 and 2.3. After confirmation the customer is addressed as {title} {last_name} (2.8).
Legal (cover mail): the agent never mentions credit reference agencies, credit files, default or court action. Questions about them get the no_info line.
OP-07 2.7 (objecting to the recording) has no dedicated line. A second objection is treated as the second 'don't want to talk' (10.6).
after_promise.ask_anything_else keeps the default (true). The brief says nothing about it.
The scam line uses the brief's own wording from 2.6 ('the back of your Kestrel Mutual card') and never reads out a phone number.
The overdraft floor is spoken as the 'minimum amount', because the brief gives it no name. The card floor is the 'minimum due' and the loan floor is the 'monthly repayment'.
Amounts are in GBP in major units (amount_scale 1), per the API.
Every tool's success is signalled by ok=true, per the API.
